t.3.66.1: But seeing the two brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, standing there, caught in the noose of his arms, Kabandha spoke these words.
t.3.66.2: Why do you two stand there, O bulls among kṣatriyas, having seen me tormented by hunger? You have been appointed by fate to serve as my food, and your senses have left you.
t.3.66.3: Having heard that, Lakṣmaṇa, though overcome with distress, yet firmly resolved upon valor, then spoke words that were timely and beneficial.
t.3.66.4: Before this vilest of rākṣasas swiftly seizes you and me, let us therefore quickly cut off his massive arms with our two swords.
t.3.66.5: Then the two Rāghavas, knowing the right place and time, greatly elated, cut off with their swords both of his arms at the shoulders.
t.3.66.7: That mighty-armed one, his arms cut off, fell with a great roar, making the sky, the earth and the directions resound, like a thundering rain-cloud.
t.3.66.6: Then Rāma, standing on the right, swiftly cut off with his sword the unchecked right arm, while the heroic Lakṣmaṇa cut off the left.
t.3.66.8: Seeing his two arms severed, the Dānava, drenched in a flood of blood and wretched, asked those two heroes, "Who are you two?"
t.3.66.9: As he was speaking thus, Lakṣmaṇa, bearing auspicious marks and of great strength, told Kabandha about Kākutstha.
t.3.66.10: This is the heir of the Ikṣvākus, known among the people by the name of Rāma. And know me to be Lakṣmaṇa, his own younger brother.
t.3.66.11: While this one, whose might is like that of a god, was dwelling in the lonely forest, his wife was carried off by a Rākṣasa; seeking her, we two have come here.
t.3.66.13: Thus addressed by Lakṣmaṇa, Kabandha, supremely pleased and remembering those words of Indra, spoke these words in reply.
t.3.66.12: But who are you, O Kabandha, and for what purpose do you, looking as you do, writhe about in the forest with a blazing mouth set in your chest and your legs broken?
t.3.66.14: Welcome to you both, tigers among men! By good fortune I see you, and by good fortune these two binding arms of mine have been cut off by you two.
t.3.66.15: And how this hideous form of mine came to me through my own misconduct, hear that from me, O tiger among men, as I truthfully relate it to you.
